memo.verdict: Park. Do not progress to Early-Stage Assessment. Medium-high conviction. Direction: bearish on progression, neutral on the equity, because a second-percentile multiple and two running EUR 1,000m buybacks make a short case unattractive while nothing yet justifies committing deeper research capital. The memo's one-line reason: the case fails on construction, not on price. The fulcrum driver, United States same-market treatment growth, is accelerating in the wrong direction, and the earnings that currently look healthy are funded by a reimbursement benefit that expires in fiscal 2027. Named re-entry conditions, all three tested together:
case: Leg one, the fulcrum driver is deteriorating monotonically. United States same-market treatment growth is the decisive variable because clinics carry high fixed-cost operating leverage and optimal margins require chair occupancy above 65%. The series ran 0.2% in 2023, 0.1% in 2024 and 0.0% in 2025, then (0.2%) in Q4 2025, (0.4%) in Q1 2026 and (0.9%) in Q2 2026. Each print is worse than the last. Management lowered full-year same-market treatment guidance from broadly flat to (0.9%) and deferred the recovery timeline from late 2026 into fiscal 2027. The chief executive labelled it publicly: "I'm the last person to want to speak to an operational miss, but clearly we have one here."

Leg two, the peer read removes the industry-wide excuse. DaVita reported positive 0.3% same-market treatment growth in the identical Q2 2026 quarter, a 120 basis point gap, and attributed half of its raised 2026 volume growth guidance of 25 to 50 basis points to patient transfers from this company's clinic closures. Management disclosed that the contraction was caused by internal sales force and business development execution failures during clinic rationalisation. The Risks report calls the divergence unexplained by general dialysis market dynamics.

Leg three, the route to market has been damaged self-inflictedly. Clinic volume depends on long-term trusting relationships with nephrologists who direct referrals, and regulation requires clinics to engage them as medical directors. About 100 underperforming United States clinics were exited in the first half of 2026, generating EUR 166m of front-loaded one-time cost in Q1 2026 alone. Those closures eliminate medical director fees of USD 150,000 to USD 200,000 annually, and frustrated nephrologists divert patient flows to alternative regional providers. Structural protections that should have held the route, 49% local nephrologist joint-venture ownership and an electronic health record used by 62% of aligned providers, did not.
counter_case: The Risks report's own recommendation, quoted by the memo and adopted rather than overridden: "Final stage verdict: HOLD current position size and DO NOT add incremental capital allocation. The investment should remain in a monitoring stage rather than progressing to increased conviction or portfolio weighting." Its stage-progression section calls for an immediate pause-and-monitor stage recommendation rather than accelerated capital deployment. The memo notes it goes slightly further in framing: the Risks report addresses an existing holder, while the memo addresses a candidate Viewforth does not own, where the bar for spending Early-Stage Assessment hours is higher than the bar for holding, so the same evidence produces a firmer negative.

Counter one, the strongest bull argument the memo carried. Waiting for capitulation forfeits the setup, since a second-percentile multiple with two EUR 1,000m buybacks running may never capitulate. The memo names this the strongest bull argument in the memo. It is rejected because the setup rubric asks for the clearing event to have cleared, and the fulcrum metric is still deteriorating quarter on quarter.
triggers: Re-entry condition one. Two consecutive quarters of positive United States same-market treatment growth exceeding DaVita by at least 50 basis points, the falsification test the Risks report specifies. Sequential improvement toward 0.0% at the Q3 2026 print in November 2026 is the first checkpoint, and it is the first reported quarter under new Care Delivery leadership.
Re-entry condition two. Explicit management disclosure of normalised Value-Based Care profitability excluding contract true-ups, which would settle the EUR 10m to EUR 20m quarterly loss question.
Re-entry condition three. Fiscal 2027 guidance that explicitly absorbs the EUR 190m reimbursement roll-off rather than deferring it, the kitchen-sink condition the clearing-event setup requires.
Abandonment trigger. Sustained euro-dollar appreciation above 1.20 on a three-month average basis, against the 1.130 average of 2025.

Monitoring items named in the memo. The CY 2027 final reimbursement rule in November 2026, specifically whether the base rate calculation includes the full USD 15.96 average-sales-price adjustment for oral phosphate binders. The quarterly cost-programme run-rate against the EUR 250m fiscal 2026 increment, with a warning threshold below EUR 200m cumulative. Medical director attrition and nephrologist referral counts as the leading indicator of route-to-market repair. A re-count of change-from-current items after the Q3 2026 print, treating a reduction below six as the threshold for re-testing the simplicity guardrail. A re-score of Element E5 (Thematic fit) at the end-of-Q3 2026 thematics review, since Thematics 1 to 3 are carried forward from April 2026 and not re-reviewed.

What would justify a kill rather than a park. Evidence that United States share loss is permanent rather than execution-driven, for example a fourth consecutive quarter of widening deficit to the peer under new leadership.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
